cues.text: A small boy with a big touch
Antoine Griezmann was born in 1991 in Mâcon, a town in France.
He played for his hometown club, UF Mâconnais.
He was small and slim, but he was very good with the ball.
Kick the ball.
Antoine dreamed of joining a big French club’s academy, where young players train to become professionals.
Every week he played, and every week he hoped someone would notice him.
Your size today is not the size of your dreams.
Told no, again and again
Antoine had trials at several professional clubs in France, including Lyon, Auxerre, Saint-Étienne and Sochaux.
Again and again, they said no.
The clubs were not sure about him because he was so small.
Being small does not make you a worse player, but some coaches worried he would not be strong enough.
Knock on the doors.
Hearing no so many times would make anyone sad.
But Antoine kept going to trials and kept playing.
Keep going after a no. One club’s opinion does not decide who you can become.
Someone was watching
In 2005, during a trial with Montpellier, Antoine played in a friendly match.
Watching was Éric Olhats, a scout for Real Sociedad, a club in Spain.
Olhats liked what he saw: a boy with great technique who seemed to understand the game.
Lift the flap.
Olhats invited him for a week’s trial in San Sebastián.
It was extended to a second week, and then Real Sociedad offered him a place in their youth team.
Antoine’s dream was coming true, but in a different country from the one he had expected.
Keep showing what you can do. The right person might be watching.
Across the border
Antoine was still a young teenager, a long way from his family.
He lived with Éric Olhats in Bayonne, a French town near the Spanish border, and went to school there.
Being far from home at that age is hard for anyone.
Unfold the bridge.
In the evenings, he crossed into Spain to train with Real Sociedad.
It was a long journey, but he kept going.
He grew stronger and more skilful every year.
A hard journey can be worth it when you love what you do.
A final at home
In 2009, Antoine played his first match for Real Sociedad, and in 2014 he moved to Atlético Madrid.
At Euro 2016, held in France, he was the top scorer, with six goals, and he was named the best player of the tournament.
Lift the rain cloud.
But in the final, France lost 1–0 to Portugal.
Losing a final in your own country is very hard.
Antoine and his teammates had to pick themselves up and start again.
Losing hurts. Let yourself feel it, then get ready for the next chance.
Champion of the world
Two years later, at the 2018 World Cup, France reached the final again.
They beat Croatia 4–2.
Antoine scored a penalty, and he was named player of the match.
It was France’s second World Cup win.
Raise the trophy.
The boy that French clubs had called too small was now a world champion with France.
He stopped playing for France in 2024.
Size is not everything. Skill, hard work and belief can carry you a long way.
